vessāmitta.notes: DN 32 names Vessāmitta among the yakkha chiefs to invoke. DN 20:8.1–2 uses the plural Vessāmittā for five hundred yakkhas. DPPN places the chief at that gathering, but the verse itself does not single him out. Claude: Vessāmitta 03 tells this very gathering of DN 20; the other entry is a sage of old.

vesālī.notes: AN 3.73, AN 8.43 and SN 1.38 are set at Kapilavatthu, Sāvatthī and Rājagaha respectively. Their cited pages also cover AN 3.74, AN 8.44 and SN 1.39, which are set at Vesālī. DN 20:11.2 refers to the city through its nāgas, Vesālā.

vetaraṇī.notes: SN 1.33 and Snp 3.10 name the river. MN 130:24.1 describes the caustic river beside the Sword-Leaf Forest. DPPN attributes its identification as Vetaraṇī to Buddhaghosa.

veṇḍu.notes: In SN 2.12 Veṇḍu speaks a verse praising those who train, which DPPN describes as a question. The neighboring citations concern Candimasa (SN 2.11), Dīghalaṭṭhi (SN 2.13) and Nandana (SN 2.14). SN 2.20:14.1 names Veṇḍu in the chapter recap.

videha.notes: DN 19:36.7 pairs Mithilā with the Videhas. The river crossing cited at MN 34:2.1 uses the form suvidehānaṁ for the people on the far bank.

vijaya.notes: AN 6.120–139:1.15 lists the householder between Sandhāna and Vijayamāhika. The Pāli reads vicayo gahapati and Sujato gives Vijaya. This accounts for the lay entry despite the missing packet mention. AN 6.119 concerns Tapussa and AN 6.140 concerns greed. SN 5.4 and Thig 6.8 name the nun Vijayā.

vimala.notes: The verse attributions distinguish the two elders. DPD and DPPN read a paccekabuddha named Vimala in MN 116:6.16, while Sujato takes vimalo as an epithet of Ketumā ('the immaculate'). The packet omits MN 116. Thig 5.2 names the nun Vimalā, the former courtesan.

vipula.notes: The packet lists no mentions. SN 2.30:16.1–2 calls Vipula the foremost mountain of Rājagaha, and Thig 16.1:50.3–4 compares a heap of bones to it (vipulena). Sujato calls the mountain Vepulla in both places. The citation to SN 3.1 shares the page with SN 2.30.

virūlha.notes: The packet misses virūḷho at DN 20:9.12, where he rules the south and the Kumbhaṇḍas. The same discourse uses virūḷhako at 9.42. DN 18:12.4 and DN 19:2.4 also use the longer form for the southern king.

virūpakkha.notes: AN 4.67 explicitly calls Virūpakkha one of four royal snake families. AN 4.66 shares the cited page. The four DN passages identify the king by his western quarter.

visākha.notes: MN 44 calls Dhammadinnā’s questioner a layman. The other three texts name the elder Pañcālaputta. The page matches AN 4.47, AN 4.49 and SN 21.8 do not name him. The remaining packet mentions belong to women named Visākhā.

visākhā.notes: AN 1.259 and the other seven laywoman passages call her Migāra’s mother. DN 14:1.12.10–11 identifies Kakusandha’s mother. Thig 1.13 names the nun, for whom the packet has no entry. AN 4.48, SN 21.7 and MN 44 address men. The citations to AN 1.248–257, AN 1.268–277, AN 3.69, AN 7.62, AN 8.48 and AN 8.118–119 do not name the donor. AN 7.63 concerns Sujātā, whom DPPN calls her sister. The chapter recaps at AN 8.50, Ud 2.10 and Ud 8.10 also mention Visākhā outside the packet.

visāṇā.notes: DN 32:7.40–41 calls Visāṇā Kuvera’s rājadhānī, his capital. DPPN glosses it as his kingdom.

viṭeṇḍu.notes: DPPN’s ‘vessels’ appears to be a typo for ‘vassals’. DN 20:10.1–3 counts Viṭeṇḍu among the Four Kings’ servants (dāsā).
